items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1826

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to enacting the "save New
York call center jobs act"

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to penalize companies that relocate call
center jobs overseas or to another state by restricting their access to
state contracts and loans.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

The bill amends the labor law by adding Article 21, which would allow
for a list of call centers that relocate to another country or state,
clawbacks on grants and incentives given to companies for a period prior
to moving to another state or country, prevents future state incentives
for any company that has moved a call center to another state or coun-
try, and the ability for the Commissioner of Labor to establish regu-
lations.

Section three sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Over the past five years, the United States has lost a large amount of
call center jobs as businesses have opted to relocate offshore or to
another state. In addition to limiting employment opportunities for
struggling families, the use of foreign call centers present a number of
security concerns with respect to protecting New Yorkers personal confi-
dential information.

In an effort to combat unemployment in New York State, this bill holds
companies that outsource jobs to another country or state accountable.
This legislation directs the commissioner to compile a list of all call
center employers in NYS that relocate jobs overseas and publicly
discloses this information to all state agencies.  Additionally, call
center employers that appear on the list will be ineligible for state
grants, guaranteed loans and tax benefits.

This measure gives companies throughout the state an incentive to
support New York's workforce, as opposed to negligently shipping jobs
abroad or to another state. It is fiscally irresponsible to continue to
reward with taxpayer dollars and state subsidies, businesses that relo-
cate jobs.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2012: S.6918 Referred to Labor/A.9809 Passed Assembly

2013-14: S.542A Referred to Labor

2015-16: S.757-A Referred to Labor, Amended, Reported and Committed to
Finance/A3688-A Referred to Labor and Amended

2017-18: S.1804A Referred to Labor
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1826B            REVISED 3/6/2019

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the labor law, in relation to enacting
the "New York call center jobs act"

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to penalize companies that relocate call
center jobs overseas or to another state by restricting their access to
state contracts and loans.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

The bill amends the labor law by adding Article 21, which would allow
for a list of call centers that relocate to another country or state,
clawbacks on grants and incentives given to companies who move call
center jobs out of state or out of the country prospectively, prevents
future state incentives for any company that has moved a call center to
another state or country, and the ability for the Commissioner of Labor
to establish regulations.

Section three sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Over the past ten years, the United States has lost a large amount of
call center jobs as businesses have opted to relocate offshore or to
another state. In addition to limiting employment opportunities for
struggling families, the use of foreign call centers present a number of
security concerns with respect to protecting New Yorkers personal confi-
dential information.  In an effort to combat unemployment in New York
State, this will ensure that moving forward, companies who outsource
jobs to another country or state will be held accountable. This legis-
lation directs the commissioner to compile a list of all call center
employers in NYS that relocate jobs overseas and publicly discloses this
information to all state agencies.

Additionally, call center employers that appear on the list will be
ineligible for state grants, guaranteed loans and tax benefits.  Simi-
larly, the state will be able to claw back tax benefits and incentives
for companies who received those benefits and moved jobs out of state or
out of the country after this bill has become a law.  This measure thus
puts companies on notice and gives companies throughout the state an
incentive to support New York's workforce, as opposed to negligently
shipping jobs abroad or to another state. It is fiscally irresponsible
to continue to reward with taxpayer dollars and state subsidies busi-
nesses that relocate jobs.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2012: S.6918 Referred to Labor/A.9809 Passed Assembly
2013-14: S.542A Referred to Labor
2015-16: S.757-A Referred to Labor, Amended, Reported and Committed to
Finance/A3688-A Referred to Labor and Amended
2017-18: S.1804A Referred to Labor

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 97 Chapter 752
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 1826-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the labor law, in relation to enacting the "New
        York call center jobs act""
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would protect New York jobs by enacting the "New  York  Call
Center  Jobs Act." Corporations are increasingly moving call center jobs
overseas to the detriment of New York workers and  families.  This  bill
will end the ability of any corporation to move these jobs while contin-
uing to reap economic benefits from the State on the backs of hard work-
ing NYS taxpayers.
 
  The  bill  requires  the Department of Labor to track all call centers
that move New York call center jobs and compile an annual list  of  such
call  centers;  imposes  severe penalties against companies that fail to
timely report such information; forces  employers  that  received  State
benefits  specific  to  call  centers  that move jobs from New   York to
another country to repay the value of any grant or guaranteed loans they
have received for the call center in the past five years; and  prohibits
those companies from receiving future state benefits for five years.
 
  Additionally, state agencies would be required to make best efforts to
ensure  that call center and customer service contracts are performed in
New York.
 
  Because the Legislature has agreed to certain amendments to the  bill,
including  the  removal  of  provisions that were unconstitutional while
preserving the original intent of the bill, I am signing this  bill  and
am pleased to advance a bill that will protect New York jobs.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Enacts the "New York call center jobs act"; requires prior notice of relocation of call center jobs from New York to a foreign country; directs the commissioner of labor to maintain a list of employers who move call center jobs; prohibits loans or grants.
